title: Feedback Unspool and Microfix Cribsheet
content:
Purpose and scope:
This cribsheet is a rapid distillation of customer feedback threads gathered July–Sept 2025, focused on small-scope fixes and probes that unblock customers or materially reduce friction. Not a full roadmap — tactical, short time-to-value items for the next 2 sprints.

Top-level synthesis (executive TL;DR):
- Many customers report repeated latency hiccups for short (<2s) interactive calls, esp when routing across regions or when caching misses occur.
- Feature asks cluster around: clearer fallback behavior, per-route caching controls, improved embedding stability for multimodal uploads, and billing/attribution clarity for batched/tokenized requests.
- Highest-impact microfix candidates: 1) explicit cache-priming flag for predictable low-latency cold starts; 2) per-route fallback transparency in logs and the Console UI; 3) lightweight SDK helper for deterministic batching in edge clients.

Representative customer vignettes and direct quotes:
- Fintech startup (seed): "We see 200–400ms spikes every morning. Can't tell if it's us or the model. If caching misses, UX breaks."
- Health platform (enterprise): "We need to pin behavior — when you fallback to cheaper model we need a notice and an opt-out. Also, token billing spikes after batching changes were rolled out."
- Marketplace (mid-market): "Embeddings drift when customers upload PDFs with images — search quality drops across batches. We suspect different preproc, or our chunking interacts with the model kv-cache."

Microfix candidates (ranked by expected impact / effort):
1) Cache-priming API flag + quickstart (impact: high, effort: low)
   - What: Add allow_prefill=true on generation/chat endpoints to prepopulate KV cache and warm model variant before user-visible response.
   - Why: Customers see cold-start latency; an explicit primitive is easier than ad-hoc heuristics.
   - Quick implementation notes: server-side toggle that runs a short (configurable) prefix against warm pool; should be rate-limited per account. Expose via SDKs.
   - Linked tickets: JIRA-CS-8813 (probe), GH-ops/142 (warm-path work).

2) Per-route fallback transparency & console annotation (impact: high, effort: medium)
   - What: Surface in Console and request logs when routing chosen a fallback model/region and why (capacity/cost policy).
   - Why: Enterprise customers demand explainability for silent quality regressions.
   - UX note: Add a small banner in per-route traces + optional webhook that posts fallback events.
   - Risk: privacy considerations if we include region IDs — consult security.

3) Deterministic client-side batching helper (lib) (impact: medium, effort: low-medium)
   - What: Provide tiny SDK helper (JS + Python) that exposes windowed-batching primitives with predictable flush behavior (max_wait, max_tokens, user_priority).
   - Why: Customers using edge devices/crazy load patterns want predictable bill & latency trade-offs.
   - Perf note: ensure the helper includes deterministic request ids for dedupe and idempotency keys.

4) Embedding preproc checklist + small normalization lib (impact: medium, effort: low)
   - What: Short doc + sample script to normalize PDFs/images text extraction and chunk size to reduce embedding drift. Provide sample config for chunk overlap and embed size.
   - Why: Many of the embedding quality asks are preproc-related; giving customers a standard reduces variance and support load.

5) Billing attribution audit trail for batched tokens (impact: medium, effort: medium)
   - What: Add a flag to request logs that maps tokens charged back to originating user/request (for multi-tenant microservices).
   - Why: Customers reported unexpected token spikes after internal batching rollout.

Notes from field triage (raw):
- Customer A: repeating "sudden cold spikes at 09:00 PST" -> likely cron jobs + cache expiry alignment. Suggested short mitigation: stagger priming requests + set warm TTL.
- Customer B: embeddings mismatch across versions after model swap -> likely different tokenization/quantization. Recommend small eval harness to compare embeddings on canonical prompt set.
- Customer C: wants ability to "opt-out" from fallback to cheaper model during canary -> propose per-customer policy flag or per-route enforcement.

Open questions and unknowns:
- Can warm priming be done without increasing per-token cost or breaking fairness for multi-tenant hosts? Need infra cost estimate.
- How will per-route fallback events tie into current Console retention & cost (we may need sampling).
- SDK batching helper: should it live in developer-experience repo or be distributed as a standalone package? (Trade-offs: release cycle vs discoverability).

Proposed immediate next steps (2-week cadence):
- Week 1: Rapid spike for Cache-priming feasibility (eng-serving-runtime + infra): measure cost delta for 1k priming requests/day per account. Owner: Marco. Outcome: numeric cost and perf delta.
- Week 1: Draft Console fallback UI mockups and minimal log schema. Owner: Leah (product). Outcome: design + privacy checklist.
- Week 2: Small SDK helper PoC (JS) and internal test harness. Owner: Evan (devexp). Outcome: repo + example app.
- End of sprint: compile a short playbook (this doc -> playbook) for CS to run customer-specific mitigations (priming script, preproc steps, routing flags).

Quick triage checklist for CS reps (copy-paste friendly):
- Is the customer on Dedicated/Private/Hosted? (affects recommended mitigations)
- Do latency spikes correlate with time/region? (check traces and priming TTL)
- Are embeddings using the same preproc pipeline across uploads? (ask for sample file)
- Any recent model version/quant change around spike window? (logs + model versions)
- If billing spike: gather request IDs & batch windows for audit.

Appendix: short templates
- Priming curl template: curl POST /v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-large-v1","allow_prefill":true,"input":"<warm_prompt>"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'
- Batching helper example (JS pseudo): const b = new BatchWindow({maxWaitMs:50,maxTokens:512}); b.enqueue(request);

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Confirm ownership of JIRA-CS-8813 and link to eng timeline.
- Ask security about logging region IDs in fallback events.
- Turn this cribsheet into a short Confluence playbook if week-1 spikes look promising.

Raw snippets from Slack (anonymized):
- "we lost a lot of search relevance when we switched to v3-quant — images + ocr seem different" — @customer-success
- "a simple opt-out for fallbacks would let us run aggressive canaries" — @enterprise-accounts

End.
